plan.intro: You're solid at Mid and already doing parts of Senior. To get there fully, build depth in testing and engineering, and take the lead in client conversations.

actions.title: Own a test strategy for the repairs pipeline
actions.detail: Write a short test strategy covering data quality, schema changes and performance, then put it in place with the team. It creates Senior-level evidence for Testing (data).

actions.title: Lead the next options conversation yourself
actions.detail: Ask your lead to let you run the next client meeting end to end, including budget trade-offs. Ask for feedback straight afterwards.

actions.title: Take the QA and testing course and quiz
actions.detail: Test Automation University's free courses cover the gaps the knowledge quiz found. Retake the subject quiz afterwards.

actions.title: Refactor the ingestion code with a reviewer
actions.detail: Pick the messiest ingestion module and refactor it with tests, with a Lead reviewing. It builds Programming and build towards Skilled.

evidence.title: Rebuilt the housing repairs data pipeline
evidence.text: The council's overnight repairs load kept failing and staff didn't trust the dashboard. I rebuilt the pipeline in dbt on the client's warehouse, splitting it into staged models, and set up incremental loads so it finishes in 20 minutes instead of 3 hours. I documented each model so the client team can maintain it.
evidence.summary: Rebuilt a failing overnight pipeline so it's faster and maintainable by the client.

skills.name: Data development process
skills.why: Designed, built and tested the pipeline from several source feeds.

skills.name: Data integration design
skills.why: Delivered the integration to agreed standards.

behaviours.name: Owning and delivering
behaviours.why: Spotted the reliability problem and fixed it beyond the original ask.

evidence.title: Designed the dimensional model for the repairs dashboard
evidence.text: I ran two sessions with the repairs managers to agree what they need to measure, then designed a star schema with a repairs fact table and dimensions for property, trade and date. I used a Type 2 dimension for properties so reports keep history when tenancies change.
evidence.summary: Designed a star schema with history for the council's repairs reporting.

skills.name: Data modelling, cleansing and enrichment
skills.why: Produced the model and chose appropriate model types.

skills.name: Data analysis and synthesis
skills.why: Turned managers' questions into clear measures.

behaviours.name: Navigating scope and complexity
behaviours.why: Broke an unclear request into smaller parts.

evidence.title: Added automated data quality tests
evidence.text: I added dbt tests for nulls, uniqueness and accepted values on the core models. They catch about two issues a week before the dashboard refreshes. I haven't yet set up testing across the whole pipeline or tested performance.
evidence.summary: Added the first automated data quality checks.

skills.name: Testing (data)
skills.why: Tests key models, but not yet a full test strategy.

skills.name: Programming and build (data engineering)
skills.why: Writes and maintains the transformation code with support.

evidence.title: Completed the Data Engineering Zoomcamp
evidence.text: I completed the nine-week course in my own time: containers, orchestration, batch and streaming. I shared my notes at the data community of practice.
evidence.summary: Finished an external data engineering course and shared what I learned.

skills.name: Data engineering and manipulation
skills.why: Growing awareness of engineering patterns beyond current project.

behaviours.name: Developing your craft
behaviours.why: Sought out learning and shared it with the practice.

evidence.title: Paired with a junior engineer on SQL and dbt
evidence.text: For six weeks I paired with Arun, who joined as a junior. We worked through real tickets together and I gradually stepped back. He now picks up modelling tickets on his own.
evidence.summary: Mentored a junior engineer until they could work independently.

behaviours.name: Supporting and developing others
behaviours.why: Gave space to deliver and stepped in when needed.

evidence.title: Presented pipeline options to the client's head of data
evidence.text: I prepared three options for moving the remaining feeds, with costs and risks, and presented them. My lead handled the hardest questions about budget.
evidence.summary: Presented technical options to a senior client stakeholder.

behaviours.name: Communicating and collaborating
behaviours.why: Translated technical options for a senior audience, with support.

evidence.title: Set up data retention rules with the data protection officer
evidence.text: Worked with the council's DPO to apply retention periods to repairs data, and added a scheduled job that removes records past their retention date.
evidence.summary: Put retention rules into practice with the DPO.

skills.name: Data management
skills.why: Applied governance in the team's products.

evidence.title: Wrote the data section of an NHS trust bid
evidence.text: I wrote the data platform section and the case study from the council work for a bid to an NHS trust.
evidence.summary: Contributed to a bid with specialist knowledge.

evidence.title: Handled a failed overnight load
evidence.text: A source system changed a column type and the load failed. I found the cause, fixed the model, told the client before their morning meeting and added a test for schema changes.
evidence.summary: Resolved a production failure quickly and prevented a repeat.

behaviours.name: Owning and delivering
behaviours.why: Kept affected people informed and addressed the cause.
